name: HOOK 1
speech: You already know you're allergic to dust mites. So why are you still coughing, weaving,
or struggling to breathe comfortably? This was the part nobody explained to me. I already knew
I was allergic to dust mites. That wasn't a mystery. I had been tested. I knew they could
make my breathing worse. So I did what you're supposed to do. Hot wash the bedding. Allergen proof
mattress cover. Vacuum. Keep the humidity down. Run the purifier. Follow the treatment plan.
I did all of it. And still, there were nights I'd wake up coughing. Sometimes I'd start clearing
my throat the second I got into bed. Other nights I'd wake up mouth breathing. Or hear that little
wheeze when I breathed out. On the bad nights, my chest would feel tight enough that I'd sit up
and wait for everything to calm down. So my bedroom slowly turned into this whole breathing
setup. AC at 68. Purifier running. Fan pointed toward the bed. Extra pillows so I could sleep
propped up. Whatever medication or spray I needed close enough to reach without getting out of bed.
I wasn't guessing anymore. I knew what I was allergic to. I was just trying to get through
the night without it turning into another 3am coughing fit. Then one night I'd done everything
right. Fresh bedding. Mattress cover zipped up. Room cleaned. Purifier running. Humidity where
it was supposed to be. I went to sleep thinking, okay, tonight should be fine. A few hours later,
I woke up coughing so hard I had to sit straight up. That little wheeze was back. My chest felt tight.
And I remember looking around the room at everything I'd bought. Everything I'd washed.
Everything I was doing and thinking, how am I still here? That was the part that got to me.
I wasn't ignoring the problem. I wasn't being lazy about it. I knew I had a dust mite allergy.
And I was following me advice, but I was still building my nights around managing what happened
when I got into bed. So I started asking a different question. Not what am I allergic to. I knew that.
I wanted to know, what are each of these things actually doing about the dust mites in my mattress?
And once I looked at it that way, it made a lot more sense. The hot wash cleans the removable
bedding. Good. The purifier filters particles from the air. Useful. The mattress cover creates a
barrier. Makes sense. My treatment helps control the reaction. I wasn't going to stop doing any of
those things. But none of them did me away to actually trap the dust mites living inside the
mattress. That was the part I couldn't get past. Because dust mites are microscopic. They live
down inside mattresses, pillows, and fabric right where you spend hours every night. And my mattress
was still sitting underneath all the washing covering and cleaning. So I started researching
what else I could do about the mattress itself. Mattress vacuums came up first. That sounded
obvious mites in the mattress vacuum the mattress. So I looked into those then professional deep
cleaning different treatments. Eventually I got to the expensive option replace the mattress.
For a minute, I seriously considered it. Get the old mattress out. Start fresh.
